title: How each topic cluster relates to the corpus's own metadata
purpose: The eight cluster specs under `_data/topics/*.json` were written by research agents who each read the material for ONE subject. That makes their material lists honest but narrow: /topics/atheism-doubt/ held 20 of the archive's 116 items, because an agent only catalogues what they read. The corpus already carries its own vocabulary - 29 post categories, 81 post tags, 28 video topics - and this file maps each cluster onto that vocabulary so a cluster page can also list the material that is ABOUT the subject even where no agent quoted from it.
why_it_matters: A reader who arrives with a question about atheism wants every argument on atheism, not only the four passages an agent happened to select. The quote-anchored material answers the question with evidence; the tag-matched material shows the reader they are not missing anything.
matching: Case-insensitive substring match of a term against a work's slug, title, post categories, post tags, video topics and video themes. Substring rather than equality because the corpus mixes 'existence of god' / 'existence%20of%20god' / 'Existence of God' across collections.

miscellany.label: Other Materials
miscellany.note: The catch-all. Anything in the corpus not claimed by a more specific cluster is listed here, so that no recovered work becomes unreachable for want of a better-fitting subject. A page of leftovers is honest; an invisible orphan is not. This cluster carries no queries and no quotes by design - it exists so the other eight are honest about their edges.

note_on_overlap: A work may match more than one cluster, and that is allowed: the person who tagged it `feminism` and `atheism` was not making a category decision the archive should overrule. The 'Other materials' card on every work page lists every cluster it matched. `/topics/miscellany/` is computed as the remainder AFTER all eight specific clusters have claimed what they match, so nothing is double-counted and nothing is dropped.
